clinician.trajectory_summary: An 83-year-old man was admitted with fever, marked asthenia, mental confusion, hypotension, and tachycardia. Laboratory tests revealed normochromic macrocytic anemia (Hb 11.2 g/dl), severe thrombocytopenia (30,000/μL), elevated LDH (2494 IU/L), CRP (5.96 mg/dl), hyperferritinemia (2656 ng/ml), hypertriglyceridemia (343 mg/dl), and positive urine culture for Escherichia coli. Sepsis was ruled out due to absence of leukocytosis, negative procalcitonin, and lack of response to meropenem. Bone marrow biopsy was ordered but results were not documented. Despite immediate HLH-targeted therapy, the patient died shortly after diagnosis from acute pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock.

Laboratory showed normochromic macrocytic anemia, severe thrombocytopenia, elevated LDH and CRP

Sepsis was excluded due to absence of leukocytosis, negative procalcitonin, and no response to broad-spectrum antibiotics
